newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Jan 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Jan 14.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Tuesday:
- The land of opportunity has meant the opportunity to defraud American investors for a small group of Russian emigres.
- American Standard Cos said it had received an unsolicited takeover bid worth $4 billion from Tyco International Ltd more than a month ago but had rejected the overture.
- Pressured by Boeing's plan to acquire McDonnell Douglas, the four partners in the European Airbus Industrie consortium said they had agreed to make Airbus an independent business.
- Mutual funds that buy stocks received a record $223 billion in net investment last year, including $13.5 billion in net inflows in December.
- Profits rose sharply in the fourth quarter at J.P. Morgan and several other large bank companies.

- Fidelity Investments, stung by criticism over the performance of its mutual funds, is sending executives out on the road to meet retail customers and representatives of companies whose employees invest in Fidelity retirement programs.
- Two of the principals in Odyssey Partners have written to investors saying they plan to shut the fund.
- A group of Marvel Entertainment bondholders asked a bankruptcy court to effectively allow them to seize control of Marvel.
- Gehe of Germany has won a year-long battle for Lloyd's Chemists, a British pharmacy chain, after a competing bidder dropped out of the process.
- A consolidation of the gene-therapy industry advanced as Novartis said it would buy the 26.8 percent of Systemix it did not already own and Cell Genesys said it would acquire Somatix Therapy.
- NCR and Computer Associates plan to encourage customers to use Computer Associates software to manage NCR computer systems.

- An Enron ad campaign will feature customers from around the world, including a plant in the Philippines, in an effort to persuade Americans to demand faster electricity deregulation, teach them the Enron name and win them as customers.
